name: Giorgio Moroder
hook: A Munich producer who built Donna Summer's 'I Feel Love' almost entirely from a sequenced Moog, which Brian Eno is said to have called the sound of the future.
blurb: Giorgio Moroder was born in 1940 in Ortisei, a German-speaking town in South Tyrol, in the Italian Alps, and worked as a producer at Musicland Studios in Munich. With the lyricist Pete Bellotte he made Donna Summer's records in the 1970s. 'I Feel Love' was made there in 1976 and 1977 with Bellotte and the engineer Robby Wedel, who showed Moroder how to lock a sequenced Moog synthesizer to the tape with a click track. Everything except her voice and Keith Forsey's kick drum came from the Moog, playing repeating patterns in exact time. It was borrowed and kept drifting out of tune, so it was recorded in bursts of 20 to 30 seconds. That sound led straight to much of the electronic dance music that followed. The best-known reaction is Bowie's story of Eno arriving at the Berlin sessions saying he had heard the sound of the future.
